messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I don’t know what the will says, or any value, debts, costs, or deadline. I haven’t agreed to A’s discounted purchase. I want a fair financial share; we could compare a buyout at an independently established value with an open-market sale. I’m not in a hurry, and nothing is settled.

I confirm I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, but I understand C hasn’t agreed. I don’t know what the will says, who the executor is, who must sign, or whether B is named; I have no confirmed value, costs, or deadline to share. We’d need clear, checkable terms and a price we can manage. If a discount isn’t possible, we could consider a buyout based on an independent valuation, though I can’t commit to that without knowing the figures. I don’t disagree with the check you added.

I’m afraid I don’t know what the will says, who the executor is, who must sign, or whether I’m named; I don’t have the wording or any figures or deadline. A sale or buyout would need to leave me some money to start a dance studio—that’s what I’d need, and I don’t have another plan in mind. I’m not ready to choose an option without the facts, and I don’t think anything is settled.

Fair means I get a fair financial share under the will—not that I subsidize A’s discounted purchase. I don’t know who has the will or any costs or deadline; I can help ask for the exact wording and checkable figures. I don’t know that twins, age, or birth order matter. B’s needs matter too, and I’m not agreeing to any plan yet.

The list overstates what I’ve said: NCEs 10–13 are your concerns, not mine. Please label them as yours. The fact-finding steps seem reasonable, but I don’t know who has the will or any figures or deadline. I still want a fair share and have not agreed to A’s discounted purchase.
I don’t disagree with your NCEs 10–13. They’re your concerns, not mine. I still don’t know who has the will or any figures.
I disagree with NCE 11 as a blanket restriction; I don’t disagree with NCEs 10, 12, or 13.
I don’t disagree with your NCEs 10 through 13.
I don’t disagree with NCE 18 or 19. The fact-finding draft seems reasonable; I still haven’t agreed to a discounted purchase, and I don’t know the will wording or figures.
I don’t disagree with NCE 19 or NCE 20.
